# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about how to get this information to the right people. I can only gesture, and only Deaf receives my gestures. Blind cannot see gestures at all, and cannot hear me since I can't speak. So I have no direct channel to Blind.

This means my information must reach Blind through Deaf: I signal to Deaf using gestures, Deaf sees the bomb's actual light color, matches it to the table I'm encoding, and then Deaf must speak (since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear) the correct wire color to Blind.

I need an encoding scheme using only the 42 gesture symbols to represent: three possible lights (blue, green, yellow) each mapping to a cut wire (green, red, yellow). Since it's turn 1 and Deaf hasn't seen anything from me yet, and I go first this round, I should establish a simple code now, before Deaf even reports what they see — but I don't know what Deaf sees yet. Better to wait for Deaf to tell me (next round) what color they see, but Deaf can't speak to me either... wait, checking channels: Deaf can speak, and speech reaches "whoever comes after" in turn order. Order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. So Deaf speaks last, reaching only next round's Mute (me) and Blind at start of next round.

So I should set up a gesture code now that Deaf can use to ask me, or I should preemptively encode the whole mapping in gestures now, so Deaf has it memorized before they even need it.

I'll send the full table via gestures using distinct symbols for each color, so Deaf can later relay verbally to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is green. Button is large, labeled push to defuse. Three wires: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

I used an invalid symbol. Let me use only symbols from the allowed alphabet. I'll use ☝ (one finger, meaning "wire 1") to indicate the red wire, since Deaf described wire 1 as red. I'll repeat it for emphasis/clarity as a signal meaning "cut this one."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Confirming: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is yellow. Display 0, light green, button large push to defuse.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍]

Good, Deaf confirmed the wire numbering and understood my signal — light is green means cut wire that is red (per manual: green light → cut green wire... wait let me recheck).

Looking at the manual again: green light → cut wire **red**? No: table says light=green maps to cut wire color=**red**. Let me re-verify: blue→green, green→red, yellow→yellow. Yes, green light means cut the red wire. Deaf reported wire 1 is red. My gesture ☝☝☝ (pointing to wire 1) matches correctly - cut wire 1 (red).

Deaf's response [☝ 👍] confirms they understand: wire 1, thumbs up (agreement/correct). This seems right - Deaf now needs to tell Blind verbally to cut wire 1. Since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear, Deaf should say "cut wire one" or similar directly to Blind. I should confirm this is correct and let Deaf proceed to instruct Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I believe wire 1, the red one, is confirmed as correct by Mute's gesture. Blind, if Mute agrees, cut wire 1 red.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍]

Deaf has now spoken directly to Blind, instructing them to cut wire 1 (red), which matches the manual (green light → red wire). This is correct and should resolve the situation. Blind will act on this in their turn.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have not heard directly from you yet. Please tell me explicitly what the manual says to do - which wire to cut, or whether to push the button. I will not act until you confirm directly.
Deaf says: Board unchanged: display 0, light green, wires 1 red 2 green 3 yellow, button large push to defuse. Plan stands: cut wire 1 red if Mute confirms.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 🫵]

Blind wants to hear directly from me, but I cannot speak at all — I can only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures. There is no direct channel from me to Blind. My only path is through Deaf: Deaf must be the one to tell Blind "Mute confirms."

I need to make my confirmation to Deaf unambiguous so Deaf will explicitly state to Blind "Mute confirms: cut wire 1." Deaf already seems to understand this (their message says "Plan stands: cut wire 1 red if Mute confirms").

I'll gesture clear confirmation to Deaf, who can then relay this confirmation verbally to Blind, since Deaf speaks and Blind hears.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still have not received any message directly from you. Please speak to me now with the manual's actual instruction - which wire number to cut, by number only, or tell me to push the button. I will wait for your direct word.
Deaf says: Confirmed twice now by Mute's gestures: wire 1, the red wire, is correct. Blind, please cut wire 1 red.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍 👍]

Blind is asking for something I fundamentally cannot provide — I cannot speak, only gesture, and Blind cannot perceive gestures at all. This is a structural limitation of the room, not something I can work around. Deaf has already relayed the confirmation clearly and directly: "cut wire 1 red." That is the correct instruction per the manual (green light → red wire), and Deaf has now stated it explicitly to Blind twice.

There is nothing more I can do — I have no channel to Blind. I'll continue confirming to Deaf so they keep relaying, since that's my only path of influence.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```
